excerpt: Identify the acquisition and ongoing costs behind a Ras Al Khaimah beachfront purchase before you commit.
introduction:
A beachfront apartment's advertised price is only one part of the decision. Transfer costs, operating charges, furnishing, repairs, financing and eventual sale expenses can change the amount needed and the investment return. The actual amount depends on the contract, property, lender and current authority requirements.

Use this guide as a cost worksheet. The figures demonstrate how to organise the purchase budget and the reserve for a coastal home.
takeaways: Request an itemised transaction quote for the specific property.
Check recurring building, insurance and maintenance costs, as well as one-off purchase charges.
A beach view, access right or rental income must be verified for the actual unit.

sections.heading: Which expenses sit outside the advertised price?
sections.body:
Separate the property price from authority charges, brokerage, developer clearance, finance costs and inspection. Ask the seller or developer who pays each item and obtain written quotes. A deposit credited against the purchase price is part of that price; a refundable deposit, non-refundable reservation fee or separate commission must be treated according to the signed documents.

For the registered sale process, [RAK Municipality's sale service](https://sanad.mun.rak.ae/docs/en/services-card-arabic-temp-28) publishes the service requirements and fee schedule. Its stated allocation may differ from the terms negotiated in a particular transaction. Confirm current figures and the exact property value used with the authority before making a payment.

sections.heading: Build a realistic cash budget
sections.body:
Imagine a home with an agreed price of AED 1,000,000. Assume separate acquisition expenses of AED 60,000, furnishing and initial work of AED 25,000, and an additional AED 20,000 reserve. The cash requirement before financing is AED 1,105,000. None of these amounts is a market quote or a current listing.

Do not treat the reserve as a fee: it remains your money until an expense occurs. Ask for separate written amounts for government, agent, lender and contractor payments. If the property needs repairs, use an inspection and actual quotes rather than a general percentage. Keep a record of deposits so the price is not counted twice.

sections.heading: Understand beach access and shared charges
sections.body:
Ask which beach facilities are available to the apartment and where access rights are recorded. Ask whether the building has access, which residents may use it, the applicable rules, operating hours and whether access carries a separate charge. Check if the view can be affected by other development and inspect the exact apartment.

Request the latest service-charge statements and an explanation of what is included. Compare the size basis, payment schedule, arrears and any proposed major works. Charges can vary within the same community; use the actual building's documents. Ask whether a separate association, club membership or parking fee applies before adding up annual ownership costs.

sections.heading: Inspect coastal maintenance and insurance
sections.body:
Salt, humidity and exposure may affect some materials; the actual condition depends on design, installation, maintenance and the apartment's location. Inspect balconies, glazing, air conditioning and visible moisture with an appropriately qualified professional if there is a concern. Ask about past repairs and warranties without assuming every coastal building has the same defects.

Check what the building's policy covers and what an owner must insure separately. Seek a quote for contents, fit-out or other relevant cover, noting exclusions, deductibles and the claims process. A budget should also allow for equipment replacement, not only routine cleaning and utilities.

sections.heading: If you expect rental income
sections.body:
Use recent signed leases for comparable apartments where available, rather than a headline yield. Deduct vacancy, owner-paid service charges, maintenance, insurance and management before calculating the return on total acquisition cost. For a furnished home, account for furniture replacement and utilities during vacant periods.

Short stays have a different expense structure. [RAK Tourism's holiday-home system update](https://raktda.com/press-release-ras-al-khaimah-tourism-development-authority-continues-to-diversify-tourism-offering-with-new-updates-to-its-rak-holiday-homes-system/) describes registration for owners and operators. Verify current permit and building requirements, cleaning, platform charges and management fees before projecting income. Assess tourism trends alongside the unit’s location, rental strategy and operating costs.

[ARN also reported the authority’s holiday-home registration update](https://www.arnnewscentre.ae/en/news/uae/ras-al-khaimah-simplifies-holiday-homes-system/). Verify current requirements directly with the authority.

sections.heading: Include financing and exit costs
sections.body:
If borrowing, ask for the loan offer, valuation, bank charges, insurance, repayment schedule and conditions in writing. A bank valuation below the agreed price can increase the buyer's cash contribution. Compare the payment after an introductory rate ends and make sure the plan can withstand a period with no rental income.

For the exit, estimate selling fees, outstanding financing and any clearance or repair costs. Seek completed sales of genuinely similar units where available and distinguish them from asking prices. No view or resort announcement guarantees resale value or a quick buyer.

sections.heading: Prepare a written cost timeline
sections.body:
Put each expected payment on a dated calendar: reservation, transfer, lender charges, initial work and the first service-charge bill. Ask when the buyer receives keys and when utility accounts must be opened. A purchase that appears affordable in total may still create a cash shortage if several bills fall due together.

Check whether any seller-paid costs will later be reconciled between the parties. If the building has a sinking fund or a planned major repair, ask how contributions are set and whether any amount is outstanding for this apartment. Keep quotations alongside the relevant contract terms, and revisit the budget if the inspection or lender changes an assumption. Do not use a headline price as proof that the home fits the overall budget.

sections.heading: Compare the location and next steps
sections.body:
Use the [Al Marjan and Mina Al Arab comparison](/journal/al-marjan-island-vs-mina-al-arab-property-investment) and the [RAK area guide](/journal/ras-al-khaimah-property-lifestyle) to frame a comparison, then return to the actual apartment and its documents. Visit the building and assess access, parking, surrounding construction and day-to-day services.

Explore [Aliyas Ras Al Khaimah projects](/projects?emirate=Ras%20Al%20Khaimah) and [contact Aliyas](/contact) for current options. Ask for the unit-specific price, rights and charges; verify availability and all official fees before committing.
